what: Same-host cost of checkpoints: retained history, checkpoint size and creation time, and a new device starting from a checkpoint against receiving every record
source_commit: 680be93315050c62a78af077d4d675f870e6871d (branch sync/checkpoint-relay; the measured code is unchanged in what merges)

host.name: betelgeuse
host.sqlite: bundled, WAL, synchronous=FULL as the app opens it
host.conditions: shared development host with other sessions; no CPU pinning; one run per workload

workload: n tasks with 1 KiB notes, a rename of every second task and a completion of every tenth, each edit its own sealed record (1.6 n records); one writer; nothing pruned
findings: A checkpoint is about 4.6-4.8% of the retained record bytes at every size measured, because sealed records carry a 3,309-byte signature each and the snapshot does not.
Retained history grows by about 4.8 KB per edit, dominated by the ML-DSA-65 signature; checkpoints add to it, as nothing is pruned.
Starting a new device from a checkpoint takes 23 ms (400 records), 99 ms (1,600) and 208 ms (3,200), growing with the collection's size.
Receiving every record from the first takes 8.5 s, 104 s and 422 s on the same workloads, growing quadratically, because each received record rebuilds the whole projection (#241).
budgets: None set: a pruning policy, and any budget on bootstrap time, needs its own approval against these figures (#40, #43).
limits: One host, one run per workload, no warm-up or repetition statistics.
Single writer; many writers add per-writer coverage entries but were not measured here.
Relay transfer time is not included: both new devices read from local bytes.
source_note: crates/matters-core/examples/checkpoint_cost.rs; both new devices are checked to hold the same tasks as the source.
